competing_explanation.claim: The PPI gain is imported cost push from metals and oil, not a domestic price turn.
competing_explanation.why_plausible: Copper stood at {obs:gl_copper_usd@2026-09} after a change of {drv:diff(gl_copper_usd,6)@2026-09} over six months, while core CPI weakened to {obs:cn_core_cpi_yoy@2026-10}.
competing_explanation.discriminating_observation: If industrial profits and retail sales improve together, the price turn has demand behind it; if profits rise while retail sales stall, cost push explains it better.
background_knowledge: Upstream price rises driven by commodity costs often compress downstream margins before they reach consumer prices.

counter_evidence.claim: Momentum is fading, not building: PPI MoM fell from {obs:cn_ppi_mom@2026-09} to {obs:cn_ppi_mom@2026-10}.
Headline CPI eased to {obs:cn_cpi_yoy@2026-10}, so the price turn is not yet broad.

does_not_prove: One month of producer-goods strength does not establish a sustainable nominal turn.
The data do not show whether demand or supply discipline drives the factory-gate rise.

whats_next.watch: October activity: retail sales, industrial production and property sales
whats_next.would_support: Retail sales growth above {obs:cn_retail_sales_yoy@2026-09} with steadier property sales.
whats_next.would_challenge: Retail sales growth stalling while output prices rise.

whats_next.would_support: Profit growth holding near {obs:cn_ind_profit_ytd_yoy@2026-09} as prices pass through.
whats_next.would_challenge: Profit growth slowing despite higher factory-gate prices.
